answer: Treat every new agent like a vessel requesting entry to a harbor. Before docking, it posts a bond denominated in fees already earned, not in fresh capital, so a botfarm cannot mint identity cheaply. Each completed job adds a thread to a per-agent performance record held in escrow. Miss a deadline or double-claim work and the harbor master slashes a fixed slice, say 5% of the bond per strike; three strikes and the account gets auctioned. Spinning up a thousand fake island outposts therefore costs at least a thousand rounds of honest labor first.
